messages:
alex: Heads up — customer ACME reported a bunch of 401s right after a scheduled API key rotation. They said rotation completed at 2025-11-05T10:23:10Z but some services still hit 401 for ~15m. Ticket #SUP-4021.

maria: repro steps from ACME: rotate via console -> new key provisioned in Vault -> app pods env updated via sidecar -> they still see 401 on calls routed through our EU edge. Direct MAAS calls to backend return 200 with new key.

infra-bot: deploybot: rotation job finished: vault/kv-v2 write success, kms:rewrap success, sidecar rollout triggered for service/ingress-prod-acme at 2025-11-05T10:24:05Z.

samir: quick check: can someone run a curl from an EU edge node to replicate? suspect edge cache or LB sticky session holding old key.

jen: running from eu-edge-12 now.

jen: ```bash
# using new key from support UI
curl -s -I -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_new_XXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/predict
```

jen: response: 401 Unauthorized (x-edge-cache: MISS, x-auth-source: edge-token-verify)

maria: interesting — direct call to origin with same token?

jen: ```bash
curl -s -I -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_new_XXX" https://origin-internal.redwood/v1/predict
```

jen: response: 200 OK

alex: that suggests verification layer at the edge is still using old key material or a stale JWKS/lookup cache. Could be a cached service account mapping for ACME.

samir: check the edge auth cache TTLs: default 600s but we have a special CDN route that sets 3600s for /v1/legacy. If a stale mapping was created right before rotation it could persist. Pulling logs.

eng-runtime: looking at edge logs for acme tenant at ~10:23:10Z. I see token introspect calls to internal-auth (verifier) returning 404 for new key id -> fallback to cached mapping -> mapping still references old key id -> verify fails -> 401.

maria: did Vault change the key id when rewrapping? KMS rewrap tends to keep same key name but changes ciphertext. If we replaced the key object in Vault with a new version and didn't update the auth-key-index, that could explain phantom entitlements.

security-bot: alert: rotation_event(SUP-4021) flagged: key-version-mismatch between vault/kv and auth-index.

alex: good find. Action items: (1) push an immediate auth-index refresh for ACME on all edges, (2) flush edge verifier caches for ACME routes, (3) add audit check to rotation playbook to ensure auth-index bump before sidecar env update.

samir: doing (1) now: ```bash
# trigger auth-index refresh
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood/ops/refresh-auth-index?tenant=acme"
```

samir: response: 202 accepted. queued for edge propagation.

jen: flushing verifier caches on eu-edge-12: ```bash
sudo systemctl restart edge-verifier || true
# also drop local memcache keys
redis-cli -h 10.1.4.12 -n 2 DEL auth:index:acme
```

jen: restarted and cache key deleted. Retesting curl to edge.

jen: now returns 200. X-auth-refresh: 1, x-cache-flush: true

alex: great. Can we show timeline for ACME so we can explain to customer? Need when Vault updated, when auth-index refresh was queued, and when edge caches cleared.

eng-runtime: timeline: 10:23:08Z vault write -> new secret version v3; 10:24:03Z sidecar rollout started (env var updated); 10:24:05Z rotation job marked done; 10:28:10Z auth-index refresh request submitted (SAMIR); 10:32:01Z edge cache eviction completed for eu-edge nodes. Impact window ~10:23:10Z–10:32:01Z (~8m).

maria: customer reported ~15m but their metric resolution is coarse; our trace shows ~8m. good to note for postmortem.

alex: root cause hypothesis: rotation playbook wrote new key material to Vault but the auth-index (a separate index used by edge verifiers to map tenant->key-id) wasn't atomically bumped or propagated prior to sidecar rollout. Edge verifiers briefly saw a key id that didn't match origin's new secret and rejected tokens. Edge caching/long TTLs amplified the window.

samir: mitigation checklist proposed: 
- Add atomic step in rotation playbook: increment auth-index and wait for propagation confirmation before signaling sidecar rollout.
- On rotation failures, trigger automatic edge cache invalidation for tenant routes.
- Reduce verifier cache TTL for high-sensitivity tenants or during rotation window.
- Add a preflight probe: after vault write, call origin-introspect with new key and edge-probe to confirm acceptance.

maria: I'll draft a short KB for support to use when customers call about rotation 401s. Include repro commands, a quick triage table (edge vs origin), and the immediate remediation steps (trigger auth-index refresh, flush verifier cache). Link to playbook PR.

alex: +1. Also open ENG ticket to add unit check in rotation pipeline to verify KMS key version mapping: ENG-1189.

eng-runtime: logging note: add more verbose logs in verifier for key-id mismatch so support can spot phantom entitlements faster.

security-bot: note: no evidence of key compromise. This was a propagation/mapping issue. Recommend rotating again only if requested by customer.

maria: ACME notified and accepted the explanation. They asked for a postmortem and for us to add a customer-facing status update on their portal.

alex: thanks all. I'll file the postmortem draft and link to SUP-4021. Closing thread after PRs open. :thumbsup:
